persistence.basis: Extreme persistence anchor: metals are elements that do not biodegrade; UNEP documents continuing mercury cycling and food-web concentration, and WHO documents lead storage in bone and accumulation over time.

extent.basis: UNEP identifies mercury as a global concern because of long-range atmospheric transport, persistence and bioaccumulation; WHO describes widespread lead contamination and exposure globally.

raw_inputs.sentinel_boundary: The generic heavy-metal node is quantified with two explicit sentinel metals: mercury for environmental persistence, global transport and food-web bioaccumulation; lead for the measured global human-health burden. The receipt is not a complete inventory of all heavy metals.

transformations.formula: Map UNEP reported global environmental mercury concentration relative to preindustrial conditions through 1×, 1.5×, 2× and 3× documented anchors.
Map WHO reported global lead-attributable DALYs through declared 0, 10, 35 and 70 million DALY anchors.
Assign the extreme persistence anchor because UNEP documents mercury cycling and bioaccumulation after release and WHO documents lead storage and accumulation in the body.
Keep mercury environmental burden separate from lead health burden; do not add them or infer an all-heavy-metal total.
0.35B + 0.30H + 0.20P + 0.15E; convert to 1–10 with 1 + 9 × composite and round to one decimal.

receipts.uncertainty: The environmental and health indicators describe different sentinel metals and assessment years. They establish a quantitative global accumulated burden for the broad heavy-metal node but must not be interpreted as a combined-metal incidence estimate or as causal attribution of the WHO lead burden to mercury. The score is a sentinel-based global accumulated-impact index, not a current ambient concentration score.
receipts.freshness: Environmental mercury inventory year 2015; WHO lead burden year 2023; reviewed 2026-08-01T00:00:00.000Z.

selection_reason.selected_method_passed: UNEP and WHO provide quantitative global environmental and health burdens, documented persistence and bioaccumulation, and global extent for two explicit sentinel heavy metals.
higher_priority_failures: No harmonized current global observation series supplies magnitude plus threshold or momentum for the full heavy-metal class.
